memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Aaron came to the altar and slaughtered the calf as a sin offering for himself. His sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and put it on the horns of the altar; the rest of the blood he poured out at the base of the altar." - Lev 9:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron does it himself. His sons assist, but the high priest's own hands take the life and apply the blood.

There is no delegation in dealing with your own sin.

Others can help. His sons brought the blood — a real and necessary service. Friends can pray with us, hold us accountable, walk beside us. But nobody can repent on your behalf. Nobody can bring your sin to God for you.

We sometimes wish they could. It would be easier to have someone else handle the uncomfortable part. But God has always dealt with people personally.

Notice too what the sons are doing. They are learning by assisting. The next generation of priests watched their father's hands and learned the work by being close to it.

That is how faith is usually passed on — not primarily by instruction but by proximity. Children learn prayer by hearing their parents pray. Young believers learn faith by watching older ones handle real difficulty.

Someone is probably watching how you handle your own failures. What they see will teach them more than anything you say.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I dealing with my own sin personally, or hoping someone else will handle it?
2. Who is watching how I live, and what are they learning?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me the honesty to bring my own sin to You directly. And let those watching me learn something true about Your mercy. Amen.
